details: CONFIRMED by tracing: sweep() (merge.py:629) takes the logged failures, then for every task worktree that removable() accepts
(merged, own commits, clean) spawns remove_child again; remove_child (569) logs the failure again on every call, so each
session start reports the previous start's failure. landed_mode (700) runs clean() for [branch] + riders(); riders() (433)
returns every wt/ branch with own commits whose tip is an ancestor of the landing branch, which a merged-but-kept branch always
is once the landing branch took the default branch; clean() returns the "kept ..." line each time. The brief's own facts
(5 of 5 landing logs ending with the kept line) are this mechanism. The item's pass case 2 says "reported once"; the item's Why
cites principle 2 (waste on every run), which the project rules rate MEDIUM for waste that repeats on every run. The new
wording names the cause and the command, which meets half of pass case 2; the "once" half has no code and no test.
evidence: merge.py:647-653  if not removable(...): continue ... going.append((path, branch)); spawn_remove(path, branch)
merge.py:576-579  reason = remove_worktree(main, path); if reason: log_line(main, "could not remove %s: %s" ...)
merge.py:708-711  for name in [branch] + riders(main, branch): line = clean(...); if line: print(line)
tests/test_land.py:772-781 (refused case) calls cleanup() once and asserts nothing about a second call.

Session 1 start: sweep finds it removable, spawns remove_child, which fails and logs "could not remove .worktrees/x: git
refused to remove it: ... run: git -C <main> worktree remove --force <path>".
Session 2 start: take_failures prints that line, the sweep spawns the removal again, it fails and logs it again.
Session 3, 4, ...: the same long line every start. Likewise every `relay land` of any later branch lists wt/x as a rider

fix_hint: Remember a refusal as a dated fact keyed by worktree path and reason (e.g. a line in the git common dir next to

spawn) while the same path still gives the same reason; or skip the retry altogether while <gitdir>/modules holds files and
name it once. Add a test that calls the cleanup twice and sees the line only the first time.

details: CONFIRMED: git's validate_no_submodules refuses for a modules/ folder OR a populated gitlink in the index; remove_worktree
attributes every "submodule" refusal to the first. Reachable only when a committed gitlink is on the default branch, so rare;
the brief listed "a gitlink in the index" as one of the causes to tell apart. Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: temp repo: git add nested (own .git) -> `git ls-files -s`: 160000 a0a7cf69... nested; ls .git/worktrees/w/ has no modules;
git worktree remove -> "fatal: working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed", rc=128.
failing_case: A branch commits a nested repository `nested` (git add of a folder holding its own .git: index entry 160000, no
.git/worktrees/<name>/modules folder). After its merge, `git worktree remove` refuses with "working trees containing
submodules cannot be moved or removed" (reproduced in a temp repo, rc=128). Now: the line says "(a repository is cloned under
its git folder)", which is false, and the --force command would delete <worktree>/nested with its own history. Should: name
the nested repository at its path (or say the cause is not known) and the step to keep it.
fix_hint: Pick the wording from what is on disk: modules/ exists under the git folder -> current text; else list index entries of mode
pass_cases: 2. A file under <gitdir>/modules: the line names the git folder's modules/ and the --force command (existing test).
3. No modules/ folder, a gitlink `nested` with nested/.git in the worktree: the line names `nested` (not "cloned under its git
findings.summary: the refusal names 'a repository is cloned under its git folder' also when the cause is a nested repository committed in the worktree
